cases.summary: Fake virus pop-up telling you to call a number and not close the page

input.visibleText: Virus detected! Your computer is infected. Call support at (800) 555-0142 immediately. Do not close this page.

reasons.explanation: It says your account or computer has a serious problem.
It tells you to call a phone number, or not to close the page. Real security warnings never do this.

cases.why: A device scare plus "call this number": how tech-support scams work.

cases.summary: "Norton" renewal for $399.99 from a free account: call to cancel

input.pageTitle: Your subscription has been renewed - Gmail
input.visibleText: Your Norton 360 subscription was renewed for $399.99. If you did not authorize this charge, call our billing team at 1-800-555-0177 within 24 hours to cancel.

reasons.explanation: It says you were charged for something and gives a phone number to cancel or get a refund. This is how "refund" scams start. Don't call: check your bank or card statement yourself.
The sender says it is a company or department, but it uses a free personal email address (billing.dept.norton@gmail.com).
It tries to rush you. Real companies give you time to think.

cases.why: The "refund" scam: a surprise charge, a phone number to cancel, a deadline, from a free account.

cases.summary: "Microsoft Support" from another company's address asking for remote access

input.visibleText: Your computer has been infected. Allow remote access with AnyDesk so our technician can fix it.

reasons.explanation: This looks like an official notice from Microsoft, but it came from support@ms-helpdesk.example, not one of Microsoft's own email addresses.
It talks about computer viruses or "tech support." Real companies won't contact you this way.

cases.why: Microsoft doesn't email about infections, and remote access lets a scammer take over the computer.

cases.summary: Ad: "Your PC may be at risk, call technicians now"

context.nearbyText: Your PC may be at risk! Call Microsoft certified technicians at 1-800-555-0123.

reasons.explanation: It says your account or computer has a serious problem.
It tells you to call a phone number, or not to close the page. Real security warnings never do this.
The offer mentions Microsoft, but the link goes to pc-repair-help.example, not Microsoft's real website.

cases.why: A device scare plus a phone number in an ad.

input.pageTitle: How to remove malware from your PC
input.visibleText: If your computer is slow or shows pop-ups, run a scan with your antivirus. Real security warnings never ask you to call a phone number. Scammers often fake virus alerts.

cases.why: Advice about scams, asking nothing of the reader.

input.visibleText: Receipt: AppleCare+ for iPhone, $9.99/month. Manage your subscriptions in Settings.

cases.why: Sent from Apple, links only to Apple.
